analysis.investment_thesis: Lloyds Enterprises is a recently-renamed conglomerate (formerly Shree Global Tradefin) that exploded from near-dormancy (₹1 Cr revenue in 2020-21) to ₹1,488 Cr revenue in FY25, but the story is undermined by an eye-watering EV/EBITDA of 78x, ROE of just 2.48%, and profits heavily propped by "Other Income" rather than core operations. At ₹9,684 Cr market cap, this is priced as a quality compounder while delivering steel-trader economics — a dangerous mismatch.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 62.72% — strong skin in the game
Revenue CAGR of 30.9% over 9 years; FY25 revenue reached ₹1,488 Cr from near-zero base
Low D/E of 0.16 (though borrowings jumped 5x YoY to ₹671 Cr in FY25)
key_risks: Market cap of ₹9,684 Cr is 5-10x outside Kedia's sweet spot — information asymmetry advantage is gone
Core profitability is illusory: Other Income (₹83-159 Cr) dwarfs operating income (₹118 Cr) — strip it out and the business barely earns
EV/EBITDA of 78.4x and P/E of 37.2x with ROE of only 2.48% — destruction of capital at current valuation
red_flags: Name changed from Shree Global Tradefin to Lloyds Enterprises in Sept 2023 — classic promoter rebranding to attract retail momentum
Net profit wildly erratic (₹154 Cr → ₹68 Cr → ₹175 Cr → ₹123 Cr) driven by non-operating 'Other Income', not sustainable earnings
Balance sheet nearly doubled in one year (₹2,396 Cr → ₹5,582 Cr in FY25) with no clear capex justification — capital raise + borrowings surge without commensurate return
Conglomerate sprawl — steel trading, real estate, engineering, gold mining, AND pizza outlets (1441 Pizzeria) signals no focused management vision
Revenue was literally ₹1 Cr in FY2020 and FY2021 — company was a shell; sudden explosion raises serious questions about business model sustainability
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a SMILE lens, Lloyds Enterprises fails on almost every dimension. At ₹9,684 Cr market cap, it is 5-10x above my preferred hunting ground where institutional neglect creates alpha. The business is a chaotic conglomerate — steel trading, real estate, engineering, mining, and pizza restaurants — with no coherent identity or moat. Revenue went from ₹1 Cr (FY21) to ₹1,488 Cr (FY25), which sounds exciting, but the company was essentially dormant for years before this, and the name change in 2023 from "Shree Global Tradefin" reeks of promoter-driven narrative packaging rather than genuine transformation. A ₹9,684 Cr market cap on a business with 2.48% ROE and 6% operating margins is valuation insanity.

The quality-of-earnings problem is the single most alarming issue. In FY22, "Other Income" was ₹159 Cr while operating income was just ₹4 Cr — the reported profit of ₹154 Cr was entirely non-operational. In FY24, Other Income was ₹135 Cr vs operating income of ₹89 Cr. Strip out the financial engineering and this is a barely-profitable steel trader with rising debt (borrowings up from ₹125 Cr to ₹671 Cr in just one year) and capital-intensive capex (₹69 Cr in FY25, rising). OCF has been positive only 3 of 5 years. EV/EBITDA at 78x is pricing in execution perfection from a conglomerate with zero track record of capital discipline — there is no margin of safety here whatsoever.
